$comment: Static fixture. The `proof` is a real Ed25519 signature by workerA (kat-keypair-003) over the 193-byte §3.1 proof_input (receiver self_aid, message_id …920, timestamp 1711900000, pop_nonce bytes 11..20); scripts/verify-known-answer.mjs and scripts/recompute-known-answer-independent.py both re-sign it. Only the envelope signature is a placeholder. `now` is the reference clock (PLACEHOLDERS.md), so the presentation is inside the RFC-AITP-0001 §5.5 window and only the nonce has expired. Extension-gated: the pinned-admission profile of RFC-AITP-0002 §3.4 is OPTIONAL, so this fixture is `status: extension` under `feature: aitp-pinned-admission`. The default runner MUST SKIP it. A runner testing an implementation that claims "AITP v0.2 pinned-admission" conformance executes it, and that implementation MUST pass it (RFC-AITP-0001 §10 item 9).
description: An expired `pop_nonce` MUST be rejected with IDENTITY_FAILED (RFC-AITP-0002 §3.4 nonce rules, check-order step 9). The verifier issued the challenge under its own AID with `expires_at` 1711899990; the presentation arrives at `now` 1711900000, ten seconds later. Its timestamp is fresh, the sender is trusted, and the envelope signature and the proof are valid, so every check before the nonce lookup passes. A verifier that keeps a nonce valid until it is consumed, ignoring its expiry, admits this subject.

expected.rationale: The nonce expired at 1711899990, before `now`. RFC-AITP-0002 §3.4 accepts a nonce only if it has not expired; the atomic lookup-and-consume (step 9) fails and the nonce is not admitted. It is not TIMESTAMP_EXPIRED: the envelope timestamp equals `now`.
